claims.text: Introducing a controlled volume fraction of incoherent or semi-coherent nanoprecipitates into an fcc FeCoNi matrix will increase magnetic-domain-wall pinning.
Increased domain-wall pinning from incoherent or semi-coherent nanoprecipitates will raise the coercive field.
The baseline can be single-phase fcc FeCoNi or an FeCoNi-based derivative containing coherent nanoprecipitates with coercivity no greater than 100 Oe.
Changing alloying elements and heat treatment can promote incoherent or semi-coherent nanoprecipitates instead of fully coherent nanoprecipitates.
Composition and thermal-processing adjustments can induce sufficient lattice mismatch while retaining an fcc matrix.
Incoherency between nanoprecipitates and the fcc matrix creates local strain fields.
Incoherency between nanoprecipitates and the fcc matrix creates misfit dislocations.
Local strain fields and misfit dislocations associated with incoherent precipitates act as strong magnetic-domain-wall pinning sites.
The increased lattice distortion and defect density associated with incoherent precipitates hinder magnetic-domain-wall motion.
Coherent nanoprecipitates introduce minimal magnetic-domain-wall pinning.
The intervention could increase coercivity to well above 100 Oe.
The coercivity increase will occur with little change in the alloy's high saturation magnetization.
The intervention can retain acceptable ductility while increasing coercivity.
The precipitate intervention can be implemented without transforming the fcc matrix to another crystal structure.
Incoherency may reduce saturation magnetization, permeability, or other soft-magnetic properties.
